### S9 — Representative local dev: `pnpm dev` on the Firestore emulator

**Superseded 2026-10-18** (never started) by [ADR-017](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-017--platform-cloudflare-workers--neon-postgres-accepted-2026-10-18): the Firestore emulator workflow it set up is gone. Its storage-contract cases moved to **S46**, its representative-local-dev requirement to **S51**.

**Gap:** Production is meant to store schedules and games in Firestore through the S7 adapter, but nothing has ever run that adapter against Firestore. The repo has no Firebase CLI, no script starts the emulator, this machine has no Java runtime (checked 2026-10-09), and S7's emulator round-trip is skipped in every run. `pnpm dev` uses the in-memory repositories, which behave differently from Firestore: they hand back the very object they stored, while Firestore returns a JSON-plain copy. A feature can therefore pass every local check and fail once deployed. `local-server.ts` runs `main()` on import, so the composition `pnpm dev` actually runs has no test. ADR-013 already says `pnpm dev` runs on the emulators; the code never did.

**Impact:** Before S9, local development "worked", but on storage that behaves differently from production. Nothing proved that a feature working on a laptop would also work deployed. S9 impact: `pnpm dev` runs the app against Google's local copy of the real database, with no cloud account and nothing deployed, so working locally becomes a reliable sign of working in production.

**Source:** Pillar: Delightful — for developers too: local development works without serious setup or a deployed cloud environment, and is representative enough that a feature that works locally very likely works deployed. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "Delightful. It applies to developers as well, and a local development experience that requires serious setup is a pain in the ass."

**Owner's requirements (2026-10-09, verbatim):** local development *"works, doesn't require its own serverless architecture that has to be deployed just for testing, and … is representative in such a way that a feature which works locally is very likely to work after being deployed"*. *"pnpm dev should be the canonical development path for running locally. If emulators are important for that, it should use emulators."* Then, having weighed a separate in-memory dev command: *"ditch the in-memory one and go emulator-only."* The owner also confirmed the Delightful approval covers this re-scope, and that CI does **not** run the emulator.

**Approach (one path):**

- **`pnpm dev` is the only way to run the app locally.** It starts the Firestore emulator under a `demo-` project ID (no real Firebase project, no login, nothing deployed), seeds it from `fixtures/` on startup, and runs the API and web against it. Data starts fresh each run. The one prerequisite is a Java runtime, which the emulator needs.
- **There is no in-memory way to run the app.** The in-memory repositories stay only as **test doubles** for the fast `functions` tests (CI has no emulator), and they are held to the same **storage contract** as the Firestore adapters so they can't drift from Firestore's behavior.
- **Projections and replay records stay in memory even under `pnpm dev`**, because no Firestore adapter exists for them yet (the *store-to-port promotion* Later theme). The README says so.

**Depends on:** S7 (Firestore adapters — `done`)

**Scope files:** `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `firebase.json`, `firestore.indexes.json`, `functions/src/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S9.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).
1. Write the storage contract (AC 1) and run it against the in-memory test doubles (AC 2). Where they differ from Firestore, change the doubles (store and return copies), not the contract. If a service turns out to rely on the old aliasing, that is a real production bug this story exists to find: fix it in `functions/src/`.
2. Run the same contract against the Firestore adapters behind the emulator guard (AC 3). Clear emulator state between cases with the emulator's `DELETE /emulator/v1/projects/<id>/databases/(default)/documents` endpoint on `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, and take the project ID from `GCLOUD_PROJECT` (which `firebase emulators:exec` sets) rather than a hard-coded one.
3. Split `local-server.ts` into a testable `createLocalServer` that takes its repositories, and an entrypoint that always uses Firestore (AC 4). Remove the `BT_USE_FIRESTORE` switch.
4. Add `firebase-tools`, the `dev` and `test:emulated` scripts, and the index file (AC 5–6); document local development (AC 7–8).
5. Set `status: done`, run `pnpm backlog:build`, update the Current baseline (the "Firestore" and "Emulator-based `pnpm dev`" rows), run `scripts/audit.sh story S9`, add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, commit.

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S9.sh` performs)

1. `functions/src/adapters/repository-contract.ts` exists and exports `describeSnapshotRepositoryContract`. The function takes a label and a factory returning `{ schedules: ScheduleRepository; games: GameRepository }` over empty storage. It seeds from the committed fixtures through `FixtureMlbStatsClient`: the file names `FixtureMlbStatsClient`, `2024-07-04`, and `744834`, so the real game with its plays is stored, not a toy object. It declares at least five `it(` cases, covering:
   - (a) a read after upsert deep-equals `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(written))`, the shape Firestore returns;
   - (b) a missing key reads `null`;
   - (c) a second upsert to the same key replaces the first;
   - (d) `listByDate` returns exactly the games whose `officialDate` matches, and `[]` for a date with none;
   - (e) mutating a value returned by a read does not change what the next read returns.
2. `functions/src/adapters/memory/repos.contract.test.ts` runs `describeSnapshotRepositoryContract` against `InMemoryScheduleRepository` / `InMemoryGameRepository`, and `pnpm --filter @bt/functions exec vitest run src/adapters/memory/repos.contract.test.ts` exits 0 with at least 5 passed and 0 skipped tests.
3. `functions/src/adapters/firestore/repos.test.ts` runs `describeSnapshotRepositoryContract` against `FirestoreScheduleRepository` / `FirestoreGameRepository` inside a block skipped when `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` is unset. With it unset, `pnpm --filter @bt/functions exec vitest run src/adapters/firestore/repos.test.ts` exits 0. It is the only `*.test.ts` under `functions/src/` that mentions `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, and `scripts/verify-S7.sh` still exits 0 (that `done` grader reads this file and `local-server.ts`).
4. `functions/src/local-server.ts`:
   - exports `createLocalServer`, which takes the schedule and game repositories (and the rest of what the API needs) as arguments and builds the API exactly as `pnpm dev` does;
   - when run as the entrypoint, always passes `FirestoreScheduleRepository` / `FirestoreGameRepository`, and exits nonzero with a message naming `pnpm dev` if `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` is unset (so it can never write to a real project by accident);
   - no longer contains `BT_USE_FIRESTORE`, and does not construct `InMemoryScheduleRepository` or `InMemoryGameRepository`;
   - starts listening only when run as the entrypoint.

   `functions/src/local-server.test.ts` builds `createLocalServer` with in-memory test doubles on port 0 and asserts `GET /health` → 200 and `GET /api/v1/schedule?date=2024-07-04` → 200 with at least one game, then closes it. `pnpm --filter @bt/functions exec vitest run src/local-server.test.ts` exits 0 offline.
5. Root `package.json`:
   - `devDependencies.firebase-tools` is an exact version (`^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`, no range);
   - `scripts.dev` contains `firebase emulators:exec`, `--only firestore`, and `--project demo-`;
   - `scripts.test:emulated` contains `firebase emulators:exec`, `--only firestore`, `--project demo-`, and `src/adapters/firestore/repos.test.ts`;
   - no script mentions `BT_USE_FIRESTORE`, and no `dev:*` script exists besides `dev` itself.
6. `firestore.indexes.json` exists at the repo root and parses as JSON with an `indexes` array, and `firebase.json` has `firestore.indexes` set to `firestore.indexes.json`.
7. `README.md` has a `## Local development` section that contains `8787`, `5173`, `demo-`, `Java`, `fresh`, `index`, and `projection` (case-insensitive). The prose those tokens anchor:
   - `pnpm dev` needs Java and nothing else: no cloud project, login, or deploy;
   - data starts fresh each run, seeded from `fixtures/`;
   - what is still not representative of production: the emulator does not enforce composite indexes (new composite queries must add one to `firestore.indexes.json`), the projection and replay stores are in-memory only, and the API runs as a Node server, not under the Functions emulator.
8. `CLAUDE.md` no longer says the local default is in-memory: its **Stack** section mentions the Firestore `emulator`, and no line contains `local default is fixtures + in-memory repos`.
9. This story's **Status** is `done`.

**Out of scope**

- Porting the projection/replay stores to Firestore. That is the *store-to-port promotion* Later theme, and S7 left it out too. The contract covers the two snapshot ports, and a later adapter joins it by calling the same function.
- The Auth emulator (**S8**), the Functions emulator, and a Cloud Functions entrypoint. None exists yet; the baseline row "Firebase Functions deploy" is "Not started".
- Running the emulator in CI. The owner said no (2026-10-09).
- Persisting emulator data between runs. Fresh each run is the design.

- Whether the Firestore half of the contract passes. Run `pnpm test:emulated` on a machine with Java and quote its pass/skip tally in the story's commit message. The contract block must **run**, not skip.
- Whether each contract case really asserts (a)–(e). The grader counts cases; it does not read their bodies.

**Re-scoped**

### S46 — Repository ports + shared storage contract + versioned snapshots

**Gap:** ADR-018: access only through repository ports — including the projection and replay stores — and one shared repository test suite run against every adapter; ADR-022: every update carries a monotonic `version`. At HEAD `GameProjectionRepository` (`functions/src/services/projection-store.ts`) and the replay-artifact repository (`replay-store.ts`) are declared in `functions/`, not `packages/ports`; the in-memory repositories hand back the stored object itself (the aliasing S9 found); and `GameSnapshot` / `ScheduleDay` carry `fetchedAt` but no `version` or `lastChangedAt`. Carries S9's contract cases (a)–(e) now that S9 is superseded. Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S46, the in-memory stores behaved differently from a real database, and nothing could tell a new game update from a stale one. S46 impact: every store is held to one shared set of behaviors, and every game and schedule carries a version so a late or repeated update can never overwrite a newer one.

**Source:** Pillar: Flexible — moving off a single-provider platform onto standard, swappable pieces behind ports (ADR-017–022). Approved by owner 2026-10-18: "The reasoning is mostly related to flexibility; I didn’t want to lean too hard on firebase when it is not as generally understood and is too tied to one provider"

(1) `web/src/api/cache.types.test.ts` line 42 writes a hand-built `ScheduleDay` literal (`date`, `windowMode`, `fetchedAt`, `games`) into the typed schedule cache key. Once AC 4 regenerates `web/src/api/generated/` with required `version` / `lastChangedAt`, `tsc` fails there (checked at `87a8375` by adding the two fields to the generated `ScheduleDay` and `GameSnapshot`: that line is the only web error outside the domain-paired fidelity test), and `pnpm verify` can't exit 0. ### S54 — Budgets in pnpm verify: bundle size, render-count harness, coverage ratchet

**Gap:** ADR-026: at most 200 KB gzipped JavaScript before the page is usable, render-count baselines for heavy views, and coverage floors of 95% (domain) and 85% lines / 80% branches elsewhere. The owner chose to ratchet (2026-10-19): floors go to today's measured values now and every story raises them until the targets are met by the end of the UI band. Measured at HEAD by the reviewers: domain 94.5% lines / 79.5% branches, web 48.5% / 85%, functions 80% / 78%; floors are far lower (web lines 14). No `size-limit`. At `58db7c2` the web build is one entry chunk of 143,833 bytes gzipped (~140 KB), so the 200 KB budget holds with ~60 KB of headroom; `tools/` (S52's lint-rule tests) is not a workspace package and has no coverage floor, so AC 3's "every package" means `packages/*`, `functions` and `web`. **Re-measured at `1967ae3` (2026-10-20 backlog review):** lines / branches / functions / statements: domain 95.95 / 87.5 / 94.28 / 95.95 (already at the 95 target), mlb-api 100 / 88.05 / 100 / 100, functions 80.01 / 78.21 / 87.77 / 80.01, web 47.35 / 84 / 69.81 / 47.35; one entry chunk of 143,827 B gzipped. `packages/ports` is interfaces only: no runtime code, no tests and no coverage block (v8 reports 0% lines for its re-export `index.ts`), so AC 3's floors apply to the packages with runtime code and ports stays without one. **AC 1's 1 KB test cannot read `web/dist`:** `pnpm verify` runs `test:coverage` before `pnpm build`, so on a clean checkout (CI) there is no `dist` yet. The test runs `size-limit` on a temp file instead, under `tools/` like S53's `jscpd` test (picked up by `pnpm test:tools`), and `pnpm verify` runs `size-limit` after `pnpm build`; `tools/` was added to the fence for it. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S54, the app could get heavier and the tests could cover less without anyone noticing. S54 impact: the build fails when the app's code outgrows its size budget or test coverage slips, and slow-to-redraw screens can be measured.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — the gates ADR-024–026 require, so duplicated logic, stale comments, slow pages and thin tests are caught by a check rather than by users. Asked whether the guardrail and budget stories may cite Dependable, as S49 does. Approved by owner 2026-10-19: "Yes"

### S59 — Web session: session provider, local dev sign-in, signed-out hides Settings

**Gap:** ADR-014 rule 7 puts session and entitlements in their own provider; ADR-027 makes Settings signed-in only (owner, 2026-10-19: "Hide settings for signed out users. Settings aren’t available without signin") and builds on the local dev sign-in now. S8 gives the server `GET /api/v1/me` with a `dev:` session; `web/` has no session concept, and the Settings route and nav item are always shown. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S59, the web app had no idea who was using it, and Settings was open to everyone. S59 impact: the app knows when you are signed in, a developer can sign in locally with one click, and signed-out visitors no longer see Settings.

**Source:** Feature: Modern membership; Settings (favorites, hide scores, playback prefs)

**Design:** S34, S56 — build to the approved frames. This story may only move to `doing` once every design story named here is `done` (rule 18; `pnpm backlog:check` enforces it).

**Depends on:** **S8** (`/api/v1/me` and the `dev:` session).

**Scope files:** `web/src/`, `web/vitest.config.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**API layer (2026-10-23 backlog review, after S49):** the web app calls the API only through the one `openapi-fetch` client in `web/src/api/client.ts` (`api.GET("/api/v1/me")`; S49). Three things follow for this story. (a) `/me` answers 401 when signed out, and the module's `unwrap` throws on any non-OK response. The session must read a 401 as "signed out" (check `response.status`), not as an error state. (b) The `dev:` bearer token goes on through one `api.use(...)` middleware in `client.ts`, not as a header on each call, so S6's settings calls inherit it. (c) Test stubs of `fetch` must return real `Response` objects, because `openapi-fetch` reads status, headers and body (S49 had to widen its fence to convert `GamePage.test.tsx`'s plain `{ ok, status, json }` stubs). `GamePage.test.tsx` (`okResponse`) and `client.test.ts` (`mockFetchOnce`) already each build a JSON `Response`. Move one helper into `web/src/test/` and use it in those files and this story's tests rather than writing a third copy (ADR-025). `web/vitest.config.ts` is fenced in so the web floors can ratchet: measured 48.07 lines / 70.37 functions against floors 47 / 69 at `87a8375` (rule 21; `scripts/verify-S54.sh` check 3 is red).

### S76 — Personal data inventory: PersonalDataStore registry, classification manifest, deletion contract case, browser-storage fence

**Gap:** ADR-028 (owner, 2026-10-23): every place BT keeps personal data must be reachable by one deletion path, enforced in code where possible and by review where not. At HEAD personal data already exists with no deletion path: `InMemoryUserRepository` (`functions/src/adapters/memory/repos.ts`, S8) holds email, display name and Patreon user ID plus `(provider, subject)` identity links, and `web/src/session/token.ts` (S59) writes the session token to `localStorage`. Nothing lists these stores, nothing labels stored fields as personal, and any file can call browser storage. S6 (settings) and S50 (Postgres) are about to add more. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-23, ahead of S6 (owner: *"Yes"*).

**Impact:** Before S76, the app could store someone's personal information anywhere without a way to erase it, and nothing would notice. S76 impact: every place that holds personal information is on one list with a way to erase it, and the build fails if someone adds a new place that isn't on the list.

1. `packages/ports` exports `PersonalDataStore` (`name`, `exportFor(uid)`, `deleteFor(uid)`), and `functions/src/services/personal-data.ts` exports one registry function that returns every registered store for the app's dependencies; the in-memory user repository (profile and identity links) is registered.

A data classification manifest in `functions/src/` labels every repository class in `functions/src/adapters/memory/repos.ts`, every field of `UserProfile`, and every adapter directory under `functions/src/adapters/` as `personal` (naming the registered store that deletes it) or `none`. ### S77 — Account export and deletion API: download first, then delete everywhere, with maximal verification

**Gap:** ADR-028 (owner, 2026-10-23): a user downloads their data and only then deletes it (*"Yes, but only if download happens before delete"*); deletion is immediate, after maximal verification including a typed phrase (*"Immediately, but with maximal verification including typing a phrase"*); and backups are handled by a deletion log re-applied after any restore. After S76 every store is registered with `exportFor` / `deleteFor`, but no route calls them, nothing checks the confirmation, and nothing records a deletion. The session (S8) is a signed token checked without a database read, so a deleted user's session still verifies until it expires; routes must not treat that as an account.

**Impact:** Before S77, there was no way for a user's data to be downloaded or erased. S77 impact: the server can hand a signed-in user all of their data and then, once they've confirmed every way we can ask, erase it from every place it's kept, at once.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S76** (the registry and stores), **S8** (session, `IdentityAdmin`), **S44** (route table).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S77.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S77.sh` performs)

1. `GET /api/v1/me/export`, signed in, returns every registered store's `exportFor(uid)` keyed by store name, plus a single-use deletion token bound to that uid that expires within 15 minutes; signed out it is 401 (test).
2. `POST /api/v1/me/delete` with the typed phrase and the deletion token deletes only when all hold, and each refusal is tested: the session was issued within the last 10 minutes (else 403, re-sign-in required); the phrase equals the one exported constant exactly (else 400); the token is valid, unused, unexpired, for this uid and came from an export (else 403, export required).
3. A successful delete runs `deleteFor` on every registered store and `IdentityAdmin.deleteAccount` for each linked identity, then `GET /api/v1/me` with the same session is 401 and no store holds anything for that uid (test). If a store fails, the request fails and a retry finishes the deletion (test with a store that fails once).
4. A deletion log records only the deleted uid and the time, and a `reapplyDeletions` function deletes a uid that a restored backup brought back (test). The deletion log is labeled in S76's classification manifest as the one entry ADR-028 keeps after a deletion (a `retained` label, which a test allows on that entry only); the single-use token record holds no personal field (token ID and expiry only) and is labeled too. (Added by the 2026-10-23 backlog review: S76's manifest fails on an unlabeled class, and `personal` would claim a store deletes the log.)
5. Both routes are in `ApiRoutes`, the spec and the web types (with their `generated.types.test.ts` pairings); `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
6. No `console.*` call in code this story adds logs an email or an export body (grep).

### S80 — Separate download from delete: stored downloads that age out in 14 days, twice in 24 hours, linked by email

**Gap:** The owner, 2026-10-27, separated download from delete (ADR-028, replacing 2026-10-23's download-then-delete): *"Deleting and downloading aren't connected. If someone wants to delete their data, they can do it without downloading. If they want to download, they can do it without deleting. If they want to do both, they have to download first, then delete."* Downloads are stored files: *"The download should be hosted in R2 with an expiration (ideally a bucket age-out policy of 14 days). If the account is deleted after that, the data is lost. If not, they can request a new download. They can request a download twice per day."* (rolling 24 hours; a link in Settings and by email: *"Both"*; deleting the account deletes the download: *"Delete them together with a warning shown and a link to the download."*). S77 shipped the opposite: `GET /api/v1/me/export` returns the data inline with a 15-minute single-use deletion token, and `POST /api/v1/me/delete` refuses with 403 `export_required` without one. Nothing stores a download, limits requests, or sends email.

**Impact:** Before S80, someone had to download their data before they could delete their account, and the download existed only in that moment. S80 impact: downloading and deleting are separate choices; a download waits for 14 days, behind a link in Settings and in an email, and goes away with the account.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S77** (the routes and deletion this changes).

**Scope files:** `packages/domain/`, `packages/ports/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `web/src/api/generated.types.test.ts`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S80.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S80.sh` performs)

1. Requesting a download, signed in, writes every registered store's `exportFor(uid)` (keyed by store name) to an `ExportStore` port in `packages/ports` with an expiry 14 days after it was made, and answers with its id and expiry, not the data; signed out it is 401 (test).
2. A third request inside any rolling 24 hours is refused with 429 and the time the next is allowed; a request 24 hours after the earliest of the two succeeds (test with an injected clock).
3. The user's current download (id and expiry) can be read, and its file fetched by its owner only: another user, an expired download, or none gets 404 (test).
4. A successful request sends one message through a `Mailer` port in `packages/ports` to the account's email, holding a link to BT and no exported data (test against the in-memory mailer).
5. `POST /api/v1/me/delete` deletes with the typed phrase and a recent sign-in alone, with no download made (test); its 403 `reauth_required` and 400 `phrase_mismatch` refusals are kept (test). The deletion token is gone: no `deletionToken`, `DeletionTokenRepository` or `export_required` remains under `packages/` or `functions/src/` (grep).
6. The `ExportStore` is registered in `personalDataStores()` as `Cloud storage: data downloads` and labeled in the classification manifest; deleting an account removes its downloads and request times, and another user's are untouched (test: the store passes the repository contract's deletion case).
7. In-memory `ExportStore` (honouring the 14-day expiry) and `Mailer` adapters live under `functions/src/adapters/memory/` and are what `pnpm dev` uses; no `console.*` call this story adds logs an email address or exported data (grep).
8. The routes are in `ApiRoutes`, the spec and the web types (with their `generated.types.test.ts` pairings); `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
9. This file’s S80 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

### S78 — Design: download and delete your data

**Gap:** ADR-028 gives signed-in users a way to download their data and a separate way to delete it, immediately, after maximal verification including typing a phrase (owner, 2026-10-23; separated by the owner 2026-10-27: *"Deleting and downloading aren't connected."*). A download is kept 14 days, can be requested twice in any rolling 24 hours, and is linked in Settings and by email; deleting the account deletes it, *"with a warning shown and a link to the download"* (owner, 2026-10-27). The ratified Settings Account section (standings-search-settings A3, S58) has "Signed in as {email}", "Sign out" and the Patreon rows, but no frame draws a way in to downloading or deletion, the current download with its expiry, the request limit, the typed-phrase confirmation, the re-sign-in a stale session needs, or what the user sees once their account is gone. A UI story can't draw a missing screen in code (rule 18). The next free standings-search-settings amendment is **A4**. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-23.

**Impact:** Before S78, there was no approved picture of how someone deletes their data. S78 impact: the owner has approved each step — getting a download, confirming a deletion by typing a phrase, and what happens after — so it can be built exactly as drawn.

### S84 — Graders prove their own story, laws hold forever: pinned re-verification, a laws registry, and every existing grader sorted

**Gap:** A story's grader is meant to prove that story's work, but nothing keeps it to that. Some graders compare the whole repository at HEAD with the state before the story (`git diff <BASE> -- <path>`), so a later story that legitimately changes the same file turns an old grader red: S81 added Playwright to the root `package.json`, and `scripts/verify-S60.sh` check 7 has failed ever since, though S60's own commit (`74a93e0`) never touched that file. `scripts/audit.sh story <ID> --reverify` re-runs a grader against today's tree, and S81's pilot recorded the owner's S60 design verdict through such a re-run, so a design verdict was tied to an unrelated re-check. And there is no list of the requirements that must hold forever: the lines BT already guards in `pnpm verify` (`bt/no-browser-storage`, `bt/no-domain-arithmetic`, the personal-data manifest test, the route-table test, `pnpm size`, the coverage ratchet, rule 22 in `pnpm backlog:check`) are scattered across ADRs and rules. The owner, 2026-10-28, on why S60's grader ran against S83's work: *"Any given story may perform work whose requirements are specific to that story's functionality, but another story might do work that directly conflicts. … We'd only want to check each test's outcomes within the scope of its work, not in the context of the entire system."* and on the model: *"The first would be an "at commit time" check which essentially proves the work is complete as defined at the time it's built, and would only be expected to succeed against the codebase as of the time of its commit. The second would be more of a law, something that defines things which ought to be checked henceforth."* Then: *"I think part of this two-tiered model change needs to be a review of all existing stories' verification passes to sort out any laws from the pinned graders. And lastly, some of the graders were modified after the original commit of the story, and I want to either reverse those changes to match the pattern as if it had existed already OR record something that notes why we did NOT change them despite the updated system."* Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-28.

**Impact:** Before S84, a check written to prove one finished piece of work could start failing months later because a different, perfectly valid change touched the same file, and nothing said which rules must hold forever. S84 impact: each story's proof stays tied to that story's own work, while a short, named list of permanent rules is checked on every change.

**Source:** Feature: Robust core

**Depends on:** **S81** (`scripts/audit.sh --design-match`, which this separates from re-verification).

**Prefer after:** **S83** (the owner put it right after S83, 2026-10-28).

**Scope files:** `scripts/`, `docs/v3/LAWS.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`, `docs/v3/LOOP.md`

**Scripts exception (owner, 2026-10-28).** Rule 8 keeps every story out of `scripts/` except its own grader. This story exists to change the graders and `scripts/audit.sh`, at the owner's direction (quoted above), so `scripts/` is fenced whole. It does not change product code or any package's tests.

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S84.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S84.sh` performs)

1. The [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract) and backlog rules 7–9 state the two tiers in the owner's words: a **grader** is a commit-time proof of its own story — every "this story didn't change X" check compares the story's own commits (its base to its shipping commit; before the commit, its base to the working tree), never the base to HEAD; a **law** is a check that runs in `pnpm verify` on every commit and is listed in `docs/v3/LAWS.md`; changing or removing a law is an owner decision, recorded like a budget change.
2. `scripts/audit.sh story <ID> --reverify` runs the grader in a temporary git worktree checked out at the story's shipping commit (read from its completion entry in `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`), never at HEAD, and removes the worktree afterwards; a test shows a grader that fails at HEAD but passes at its shipping commit re-verifies as passing.
3. A design-match verdict is recorded on its own — `scripts/audit.sh design <ID> --design-match -` — without running the story's grader; `audit.sh story`'s completion still requires the verdict for a UI story (rule 22). A test shows both.
4. `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists every law: a short statement, its source (the owner's words, an ADR or a backlog rule), and where it is enforced (the file and the `pnpm verify` step that runs it). Seeded with at least: browser storage only in `web/src/storage/` (`bt/no-browser-storage`), no arithmetic over BT data in views (`bt/no-domain-arithmetic`), every repository labeled in the personal-data manifest, dispatched routes equal `ApiRoutes`, the 200 KB entry budget (`pnpm size`), coverage floors never fall (rule 21), no copy-paste (`pnpm dup:check`), and every UI story carries a design match (rule 22). `pnpm backlog:check` (or a vault test) fails when a listed enforcement file is missing or its step is not in the `verify` chain. A seeded law that `pnpm verify` does not enforce yet is listed as **proposed**, as AC 5 allows (2026-10-28 backlog review: rule 21's "never lower a floor" has no step — `pnpm test:coverage` enforces each floor, nothing checks a floor was not lowered), and the check skips proposed rows.
5. **Every existing grader sorted** (owner: *"a review of all existing stories' verification passes to sort out any laws from the pinned graders"*). A table in `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists every check of every `scripts/verify-S*.sh` and `scripts/verify-V*.sh` (the vault-migration stages, whose completion entries are in `docs/v3/VAULT-MIGRATION-AUDIT.md`) as **pinned** or **law**. A check classed as a law is either already enforced in `pnpm verify` (named in its row) or listed as **proposed**, with what would enforce it, for a later story — this story adds no product tests. Every pinned check that compares a path with a fixed base at HEAD (`git diff <BASE> -- …`) is rewritten to compare the story's own commits.
6. **Graders edited after their story shipped** (owner: *"either reverse those changes to match the pattern as if it had existed already OR record something that notes why we did NOT change them"*). For each `scripts/verify-S*.sh` and `scripts/verify-V*.sh` with a commit after its story's completion entry, the table records the commit(s) and either restores the grader to what it would have been under the pinned model, or records why it was left as it is. Edits made before the story's completion (its own checkpoints) are not counted.
7. ### S87 — The deletion cookie: the server remembers a deleted account once, for its Settings page, and cookies come from one codepath

**Gap:** The owner wants the deletion message shown at `/settings`, *"triggered by visiting the settings page with a server-only cookie that is only sent to users after deletion"* (2026-10-29), shown *"Until seen once"*. A cookie the page's code can't read (`HttpOnly`) has to be set and read by the server: today `POST /api/v1/me/delete` sets no cookie, `GET /api/v1/me` answers a deleted user plain 401, and BT sets no cookies at all. The owner also made the cookie law a conscious choice (asked whether LAWS.md should gain it: *"Yes, add it with S87"*): cookies are set by one codepath only. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29.

**Impact:** Before S87, nothing could tell a browser that had just deleted its account apart from any signed-out visitor. S87 impact: right after a deletion the server remembers it once, privately, so Settings can show the deletion message on the next visit and then forget it — and any other cookie fails the build until the owner decides otherwise.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Depends on:** **S77** (the delete route).

1. A successful `POST /api/v1/me/delete` sets one cookie, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, `Secure` when the request came over HTTPS and not on plain `http://` (owner, 2026-10-29: *"Secure on HTTPS only"* — Safari drops `Secure` cookies on `http://localhost`), with no `Max-Age` or `Expires` (a browser-session cookie), named in one module (`functions/src/services/cookies.ts`); a refused deletion (400, 401, 403) sets none (test).
2. `GET /api/v1/me` with that cookie and no session — no bearer, an invalid one, or one whose account is gone — answers 401 with `error: "account_deleted"`; **any** `/me` response that sees the cookie clears it (`Max-Age=0`), signed in or not, so a second request answers plain 401 (*"Until seen once"*) and a signed-in request still answers 200 while discarding it (owner, 2026-10-29, asked whether a re-sign-in drops the message: *"Drop it (clear on any /me)"*) (test). The spec documents `account_deleted` on `/api/v1/me`'s 401, and the web types are regenerated; `pnpm api:breaking` exits 0.
3. **Law P10, enforced** (owner, 2026-10-29: *"Yes, add it with S87"*): a functions test fails when any API response sets a cookie other than through `cookies.ts` (checked over the route table's responses), and `docs/v3/LAWS.md` lists P10 as enforced with its file and step.

- **Ground truth:** S77 is `done`. `functions/src/handlers/api.ts` has `GET /api/v1/me` (`if (!account) return unauthorized()`, body `error: "unauthorized"`) and `POST /api/v1/me/delete` (400 `invalid_body` / refusal, 200 `{ deleted: true }`). Handlers return a web `Response`, so the cookie is a header on it, and the same code serves the Worker (S45). Nothing in `functions/src`, `packages/` or `web/src` sets or reads a cookie yet. `docs/v3/LAWS.md` has no P10 row (the owner removed the example on 2026-10-28). `scripts/backlog-vault/laws.test.ts` requires an enforced law's `Enforced by` file to exist and its `Step` to be in the `pnpm verify` chain, so a functions test is step `test:coverage`. `ApiErrorResponse.error` is a plain string in `openapi/bt-api.v1.json`, so documenting `account_deleted` breaks nothing.
- **The local Node adapter keeps one `Set-Cookie`.** `functions/src/adapters/node/http.ts` writes `Object.fromEntries(response.headers)`, which merges repeated headers. That is fine for the one cookie this story sets or clears per response. If any response ever needs two, use `headers.getSetCookie()` there; the file is inside this fence.
- **Fit with the SPA:** the API is same-origin (`baseUrl: location.origin`; in dev the Vite proxy passes `Set-Cookie` through, and with no `Domain` the cookie belongs to the page's host). A `SameSite=Strict` cookie goes with the page's own `fetch` even when the visit started from an outside link. A browser-session cookie fits *"Until seen once"*: closing the browser before visiting only loses a one-time message. The client changes S79 needs (calling `/me` with no token, reading the 401 body, one in-flight call under `StrictMode`) are in S79's notes, not here.
- **Personal data (ADR-028):** a fixed marker (AC 4) set after the uid is gone is not a store in ADR-028's inventory. It carries no personal field, it can't be traced back to the account, and it is cleared the first time it is read. Say so in `cookies.ts`'s comment and add no manifest entry. A value that identifies the account would need the owner to amend ADR-028 first.
- **P10 binds later work:** any later cookie (for example, a server-side sign-in callback when Logto lands) must go through `cookies.ts` or come with the owner's override (`docs/v3/LAWS.md` Overrides). The law's row should say so, so the story that brings the next cookie finds it.

**Status:** `done`

### S79 — Download and delete your data in Settings: stored download link, typed-phrase confirmation, immediate deletion

**Gap:** ADR-028: a signed-in user can download their data and, separately, delete it, immediately, after maximal verification including typing a phrase (owner, 2026-10-23; separated 2026-10-27: *"Deleting and downloading aren't connected."*). S77 and S80 give the server the download and delete routes, with downloads kept 14 days and limited to two in any rolling 24 hours; S78 draws the flow in standings-search-settings A4; S6 builds the Settings page it lives on. The web app has no way to reach any of it, and after a deletion the browser would still hold the session token and cached settings that S76 labeled personal.

**Impact:** Before S79, a user had no button to get their data or erase it. S79 impact: from Settings, a signed-in user can get a download of everything BT holds about them, and can type a phrase to have their account and data erased at once — including what was saved in their browser.

**Source:** Feature: Delete your data

**Design:** S34, S58, S78, S86 — build to the approved frames. This story may only move to `doing` once every design story named here is `done` (rule 18; `pnpm backlog:check` enforces it).

**Notes (2026-10-25 backlog review, after S77 and S6):**

- **Superseded by S80 (owner, 2026-10-27): the deletion token, `export_required` and the inline `GET /api/v1/me/export` go; use the routes S80 ships.** The API as S77 shipped it: `GET /api/v1/me/export` → `MeExportResponse { stores, deletionToken, deletionTokenExpiresAt }`; `POST /api/v1/me/delete` takes `MeDeleteRequest { phrase, deletionToken }` → `{ deleted: true }`. Refusals by `error`: 401 (signed out or account gone), 400 `invalid_body`, 400 `phrase_mismatch`, 403 `reauth_required` (sign-in older than 10 minutes), 403 `export_required` (token missing, used, expired or another user's). Compare the typed text against `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PHRASE` from `@bt/domain`, never a second copy (ADR-025).
- **Client:** add the two calls to `web/src/api/client.ts` beside `saveSettings` (`api.GET`, `api.POST`; inside `web/src/`). `unwrap` throws a generic error on any non-OK status, so the delete call must read the 403 body's `error` to tell `reauth_required` apart, and the download request must read S80's 429 for the next allowed time, the way `fetchMe` special-cases 401. 
- **Don't let the export linger:** signing out removes only queries under `ACCOUNT_QUERY_KEY`, so key the current-download query under it; never a query outside it. If the file is saved through a blob, jsdom has no `URL.createObjectURL`, so the test stubs it.
- **AC 5 reuses sign-out:** `useSession().signOut()` (`web/src/session/SessionProvider.tsx`) already drops the token, runs `clearPersonalData()`, removes `ACCOUNT_QUERY_KEY` queries and, through `SettingsSync`, resets the settings store. Call it after `{ deleted: true }` instead of listing keys again. Locally, a stored `dev:test-user` token re-creates the account on its next request (`functions/src/services/accounts.ts` `authenticate`), so the token has to be gone before anything refetches `/api/v1/me`.
- **AC 4 in dev:** a `dev:` bearer signs in fresh on every request, so `reauth_required` never fires against `pnpm dev`; the RTL test mocks the 403. 
- **Test setup:** a Mantine `Modal` or other floating element works in jsdom with S6's `web/src/test/setup.ts` stubs (ResizeObserver, `:popover-open` / `:modal`). `SettingsPage` takes `variant` from S60's layout host (`AppShellLayout` → `AppRoutes`); don't read the viewport in the page.
- **Personal data (ADR-028):** no new store, browser key or log line; the downloaded file is the user's own copy. If the flow keeps anything in browser storage, it is a labeled personal key in `web/src/storage/`.

- **How the SPA reaches S87's signal: four things in `web/src/` stand in the way at `aec31e6`, all inside this fence.** (1) `SessionProvider` never calls `GET /api/v1/me` without a stored token (`useState(() => getSessionToken() ? loading : SIGNED_OUT)`), and after deletion `signOut()` drops the token. (2) `fetchMe` turns every 401 into `null`, so it never reads `error: "account_deleted"`. The cookie is cleared by whichever `/me` arrives first, so if two calls race, the one whose result is used can get a plain 401 and A5 never shows. Ask once per page load, through one shared in-flight promise, only on a signed-out `/settings` (and right after a successful delete, without leaving `/settings`). A plain 401 redirects as before. The cookie itself needs nothing from the client: `openapi-fetch` builds a same-origin `Request` (`baseUrl: location.origin`, credentials `same-origin`), and the Vite proxy forwards `Set-Cookie` unchanged because S87's cookie has no `Domain`.

### S82 — Every account has an email: no null email on the account, the session or the identity claims

**Gap:** The account's email is optional everywhere: `UserProfile.email` (`packages/domain/src/types.ts`), the `/api/v1/me` response (`packages/domain/src/api-routes.ts`), and `IdentityClaims.email` / `IdentityAccount.email` (`packages/ports/src/auth.ts`) are all `string | null`, and the download service skips the ready email when it is null (`functions/src/services/data-downloads.ts`). Asked what A4's "and we emailed you the link too" should say for an account with no email, the owner answered (2026-10-28): *"It should be impossible for an account to have no email."* Inserted by the 2026-10-28 design intake review.

### S62 — Load-time budgets and end-to-end flows in CI: Lighthouse CI + Playwright

**Gap:** ADR-026: Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5 s (tiered since 2026-10-29: see the budget change below), Total Blocking Time (the lab stand-in for Interaction to Next Paint) < 200 ms and layout shift < 0.1 on a throttled mid-range phone, median of 3–5 runs, in CI; Playwright flows over the main paths against fixtures. The owner approved Lighthouse CI (2026-10-19, ADR-026) and Playwright in CI (2026-10-19). `ci.yml` runs neither. Placed right after the shell so the budgets guard the UI band while it is built. Inserted by the 2026-10-19 design intake review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Budget change (owner, 2026-10-29):** the Largest Contentful Paint budget is tiered — warn over 2.5 s, block at 5 s (ADR-026 amendment, AC 1). The first real run measured 3.19 s on both pages; "we can figure out the problems later".

**Impact:** Before S62, nobody would learn a page had become slow on a phone until users felt it. S62 impact: every change is timed on a mid-range phone profile and clicked through the main paths. ### S74 — Offline reading: stored copies, age marker, open-time prefetch, background refresh

**Gap:** ADR-023: anything already viewed stays readable offline, marked with its age; on open (and on any background wake) today's scoreboard and favorite teams' games are prefetched; Periodic Background Sync where the browser offers it; offline copies obey Hide Scores exactly like live views; the service worker stores the latest copy it was given and never decides freshness (ADR-014 rule 3). Favorites exist only for signed-in users (ADR-027). **S55 ratified 2026-10-21** (`shell-scoreboard/amendments/A1.md`, `game-rooms/amendments/A1.md`) draws the offline marker. ### S89 — Faster CI: parallel jobs, flows on several workers, design captures out of pnpm e2e

**Gap:** CI's one `build` job runs `pnpm verify`, the API checks, the Playwright flows and Lighthouse one after another (run 40932706098: verify 1m32s, flows 2m27s before failing). `e2e/playwright.config.ts` pins `workers: 1` because the design captures share one `pnpm dev` server and in-memory data (sign-in, settings, account deletion); `pnpm e2e` runs every spec under `e2e/`, so CI also retakes all the design captures, not only the flows. Asked whether the tests can run on several workers on GitHub, the owner answered (2026-10-29): *"Let's set that aside for now, maybe make a story for it"*. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29.

**Impact:** Before S89, every push waits for each CI check in turn, and the browser checks also retake every design screenshot. S89 impact: the checks run side by side, so a push learns whether it is green sooner.

**Source:** Pillar: Delightful — faster checks on every change, for performance and customer benefit; the pillar covers developers too. Approved by owner 2026-10-29: "It's more about perf and customer benefit", then, asked whether to cite Delightful or Dependable: "Delightful"

**Depends on:** **S62** (the CI job, `pnpm e2e`, `pnpm lighthouse`).

**Scope files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lighthouserc.json`, `e2e/`, `package.json`, `scripts/backlog-vault/`, `docs/v3/LAWS.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S89.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** changing CI (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S89.sh` performs)

1. `ci.yml` runs `pnpm verify` (with the API spec checks), the Playwright flows, and Lighthouse as separate jobs that start together; Lighthouse still runs alone on its runner, so nothing else shares the machine it times.
2. `pnpm e2e` runs only `e2e/flows/` (and the harness's own checks), not the design captures; `pnpm design:capture <spec>` still takes them; and CI still runs every `e2e/design/` spec, without `BT_DESIGN_CAPTURE` (so nothing is written to the tree), in its own job beside the others, so a capture spec that breaks still fails CI.
3. The flows run with more than one Playwright worker; each test that signs in or changes data gets its own state, so no flow depends on another's order (a run with `--repeat-each=2` passes).
4. **Lighthouse starts when the app is ready, not after a timeout** (owner, 2026-10-29, asked whether S89 should also fix it: *"Yes"*): in CI, `lhci` no longer logs "Timed out waiting for the server to start listening" — it sees the server's ready line (or `lighthouserc.json` waits on a check that does), so no run waits out `startServerReadyTimeout`.
5. Law P11 still holds: the vault test that reads `ci.yml` finds a step running `pnpm verify`.

### S90 — Next-pitch model: training data, a trained model, and an honest evaluation

**Gap:** BT has every pitch of the games it records (`GameSnapshot.plays`: type, call, count, location, kinematics) but nothing that learns from them. Inserted by the owner, 2026-10-29: *"I want to make a story to use pitch data to train a model or a fine tune to predict the next pitch during games"*; asked how, the owner chose *"Train our own small model"* over an LLM fine-tune.

**Impact:** Before S90, BT can only show pitches after they're thrown. S90 impact: BT has a model that, given the game situation, gives the odds of each pitch type and where it's likely to go — and a measured answer to whether it beats simply guessing the pitcher's usual pitch.

**Source:** Feature: Next-pitch prediction

**Depends on:** **S63** (the replay fold that turns MLB's recordings into `GameSnapshot.plays`).

**Scope files:** `scripts/pitch-model/`, `packages/domain/src/pitch-model.ts`, `packages/domain/src/pitch-model.test.ts`, `packages/domain/src/index.ts`, `fixtures/pitch-model/`, `docs/v3/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `package.json`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S90.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing the model (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S90.sh` performs)

1. **An ADR for the model** is proposed in `docs/v3/ARCHITECTURE.md` and accepted by the owner (quoted): where training runs (offline, on a developer machine or CI — never on a request), the training toolchain (inside the locked TypeScript stack, or the case for an exception), the model's file format, and how the Worker evaluates it with no ML runtime of its own (e.g. trees or weights evaluated in plain TypeScript).
2. **Training data** comes from MLB's own pitch-by-pitch recordings via the existing ingest path, never scraped pages: `pnpm pitch-model:collect` records past seasons offline (`BT_USE_LIVE_MLB=1`), folds them with the S63 replay fold, and writes one row per pitch — features known *before* the pitch (pitcher, batter side, count, outs, runners, inning, score margin, the pitcher's previous pitches in the at-bat and his season mix so far) and the label (pitch type, plate location). A small committed sample under `fixtures/pitch-model/` keeps tests offline.
3. **No future leaks into a prediction:** a test shows every feature for pitch *n* is computed from pitches before *n* only, and training / test splits are by date (train on earlier games, test on later ones).
4. **The model** is one named, tested function in `packages/domain` (`predictNextPitch(situation, model) → { types: { type, probability }[]; location: { pX, pZ, spread } }`): pitch-type probabilities sum to 1; the location is a likely spot with its spread.
5. **An honest evaluation** in `scripts/pitch-model/eval.md`, regenerated by `pnpm pitch-model:eval` on the held-out games: log loss and top-1 accuracy for pitch type, and location error, each beside the **baseline** of the pitcher's own pitch mix in that count. The script fails if the model doesn't beat the baseline on pitch type.
6. The model file is small enough to ship to the Worker (target under 1 MB) and `predictNextPitch` runs in under a millisecond per pitch (timed in the test).
7. This file's S90 **Status** (story heading and top table) is `done`.

**Notes:**

- **Ask before recording.** Recording past seasons pulls a lot from MLB; how many seasons, and how often to retrain, are the owner's to set — ask before the first large `collect` run.
- **Paid tier** (owner, 2026-10-29) applies to showing predictions (S91), not to training.

**Reuse check** (ADR-025): before writing code, search `packages/domain` (`pitchOutcome`, `pitcherLine`, `breakInches`, `coordinates.ts`) and `packages/mlb-api` (the replay fold, `scan-drift`) for what this story needs; record what was reused, or why nothing fit, in the story's ledger notes.

### S103 — Ingest Baseball Savant's per-pitch game feed (what MLB's feeds lack)

**Gap:** Baseball Savant's game feed (`https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/gf?game_pk=823823`; owner, 2026-10-30: *"oh, I forgot, there's also this"*) holds every pitch keyed by the live feed's `playId` (340 of 340 on 823823). Most of it repeats MLB's live feed exactly — the trajectory (`x0`…`az`, spin, breaks, extension, plate time), the strike zone, the box score and season lines — but some is in no MLB feed BT reads: per batted ball expected batting average (`xba`), barrel, spray position in feet and how many ballparks a home run leaves (`homeRunBallparks`); bat speed on every swing; sword swings; Savant's in-zone call; times through the order; the exact ABS-challenged pitch; and the location where the pitch crosses the front of the plate. BT keeps only those (owner, 2026-10-30, asked whether to ingest only what BT doesn't already have: *"Yes re: S103"*). Nothing in the feed says when Savant computed them (owner, 2026-10-30: *"Something that needs to be accounted for is the potential difference in arrival time for the baseball savant details. Since the season is over, I can't tell whether there's any time delta in the realtime arrival of these, unless the data itself tells us something useful."*) — it says only that it is built from MLB's game feed and cached (`"source": "gamefeed"`, `cacheKey`).

**Impact:** Before S103, BT knew how a pitch moved but not what Savant makes of it. S103 impact: each pitch carries Savant's extras — how likely a batted ball was to be a hit, the swing's speed, whether a home run would have left other parks — filling in as Savant publishes them, without ever holding up the live game.

**Source:** Feature: More MLB game data

**Depends on:** **S48** (the per-game ingest object that owns when MLB is called during a game; AC 5 runs inside it).

**Scope files:** `fixtures/`, `packages/mlb-api/src/`, `packages/ports/src/`, `packages/domain/src/`, `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `openapi/`, `web/src/api/generated/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/SAVANT-DATA.md`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S103.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** building (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S103.sh` performs)

1. `fixtures/raw/savant-gf-823823.json` holds Savant's response to `https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/gf?game_pk={gamePk}` for 823823, recorded once with `BT_USE_LIVE_MLB=1` and committed; tests and local dev read it, never the network.
2. `packages/mlb-api` types the pitch rows as named interfaces and parses them with zod; a parse test runs on the recording, and `pnpm mlb:scan-drift` covers it.
3. `MlbStatsClient` gains `fetchSavantGameFeed(gamePk)`, in the fixture and HTTP adapters (Savant's host as its own base URL); ingest owns the call, no web code fetches it.
4. **Only what MLB's feeds lack.** A mapper projects each pitch, joined by `playId`, into `GameSnapshot.savant` with exactly: `xba`, `isBarrel`, spray `x` / `y` in feet, `homeRunBallparks`, `batSpeed`, `isSword`, `savantInZone`, `timesThroughOrder`, `isAbsChallenge`, and the front-of-plate location (`plateXPoly`, `plateZPoly`); no trajectory, zone, box-score or season field is copied (grep over the mapper), so each value keeps one source (ADR-025). On 823823: 52 batted balls carry `xba`, 150 swings carry `batSpeed`, 2 pitches are swords, and the 5 ABS-challenged pitches are in `atBatIndex` 34, 39, 69, 82, 83 (Savant's `ab_number` is one higher) (tests). Additive to the payload (`pnpm api:breaking` exits 0).
5. **Arrival time is accounted for** (owner, 2026-10-30, quoted in the Gap):
   - Savant is pulled on its own cadence inside S48's ingest object, never in the same call as the live feed, so a slow or failing Savant never delays a pitch (test with a hanging Savant fake);
   - each Savant field is empty until it arrives and is merged into its pitch by `playId` as it does, a newer value replacing an older one only by version (ADR-022), and views read an absent field as "not yet", never as zero (unit tests on the merge);
   - for each pitch BT records when each Savant field first appeared beside the live feed's time for that pitch (`playEndTime`), so the real delay can be read once live games resume (test on a two-poll sequence);
   - polling is bounded: at most every N seconds while the game is in its live window (N in config) and once more after the final for late fields (test).
6. The source is optional: when Savant fails or returns nothing, `savant` is absent and the game is served as before (test).
7. **Terms of use first** (owner, 2026-10-30, asked whether one story should check Savant's terms of use before any live Savant call ships, covering the data, the field drawings and query-engine use, as a requirement on the first Savant story: *"Sure"*). Playwright exits nonzero with "No tests found" when the file is missing, which AC 3 can lean on, but check the file first for a clear message.

## Data platform — MLB access & types

v2’s `baseball-theater-engine` (contracts + `MlbDataServer`) is **not** copied as a package — **do not reuse v2 source types**. Rebuild the *capability* behind ports: typed upstream payloads → mappers → BT domain → fixture + live adapters (ADR-001 / ADR-012). Do **not** reintroduce browser→proxy→MLB.

**Type design (required for S11+):**

- **Every nested object gets its own named type** — no inline `{ … }` object literals as field types in the exported `interface` / `type` definitions. (The zod parsers may nest `z.object(...)` inline as much as is convenient — runtime validation shape is not the constraint; the exported *types* are.) Inlining a type is allowed only where **specifically defensible** (a genuine one-off 1–2 field wrapper) and marked with a `// design-exception:` note.
- Names must reflect **purpose** (`PitchCoordinates`, `LiveGamePlayEvent`, `ScheduleGameTeam`, …), be **intelligently separable** into modules by concern (live feed, schedule, content, standings, players), and stay **usable** — no sprawling 60-character names, no 900 near-identical types. When shapes overlap, **compose**: `extends`, unions / discriminated unions, `Pick` / `Omit`, a shared base, or a small generic — whichever fits, not copy-paste variants.
- Upstream MLB types stay separate from BT product domain (`GameSnapshot`, etc.).
- Recorded payloads are modeled to near-total field coverage behind a mechanical gate (**S23**); unknown / newly seen fields stay discoverable (**S15**), never silently dropped without a report.

### S11 — MLB upstream payload types for carried loop

**Gap:** Domain has product snapshots (`GameSnapshot`, `AtBat`) but no typed Stats API live-feed / schedule / content shapes to parse against. Hand-authored fixtures skip that layer.

**Impact:** Before S11, the app only understood the small, hand-shaped practice games used for local testing — it had no real definition of what MLB's actual data looks like. S11 impact: the app now has real, typed definitions for MLB's schedule, live-game, and highlight data — the foundation every later data feature is built on.

### S23 — Full-fidelity upstream types for the recorded fixtures

**Gap:** S11 typed only the fields the carried loop binds to, and `packages/mlb-api` uses plain `z.object()` which **silently strips** everything else — so large branches of every payload are unmodeled: `liveData.boxscore` player stat lines (`stats.batting` / `pitching` / `fielding`, `seasonStats`, `battingOrder`, `info`, `note`, `teamStats`), `gameData.flags` / `review` / `gameInfo` / `weather` / `moundVisits` / `officialScorer` / `alerts`, schedule hydrate extras, content editorial detail. Target: model the recorded payloads to **near-total field coverage**, authored from scratch in the S11 style, held in place by a mechanical coverage gate — i.e. at least as complete as v2's `baseball-theater-engine` contracts without copying them.

**Impact:** Before S23, the app's understanding of MLB's data only covered the handful of fields early features needed — large parts of every game (full box scores, weather, official reviews, and more) were quietly being thrown away. S23 impact: the app now understands nearly everything MLB sends, and an automatic check will flag it if a future MLB payload has something new and unmodeled instead of silently dropping it.

**Source:** Feature: Game → Box score; Game → Plays + pitch detail

**Depends on:** S11, S12. Picks up `fixtures/raw/live-823823-base.json` and `fixtures/raw/diffpatch-823823.json` too if S22 has landed them.

**No new recording:** every payload family in scope is already present in committed fixtures — `liveData.boxscore` (full), `gameData.*` branches, `leaders`, `decisions` in `fixtures/raw/live-823823.json`; hydrate extras in `fixtures/raw/schedule-2026-09-05.json`; editorial/highlight detail in `fixtures/raw/content-823823.json`. If a family v2 covered turns out to be absent from these, **stop and report** — that is a scoping fix, not a fence to widen.

**Scope files:** `packages/mlb-api/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S23.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S23.sh` performs)

1. `packages/mlb-api/src/` exports a coverage helper (e.g. `coverage.ts` with `leafPaths(value)` returning array-index-normalized leaf key-paths — every numeric index rendered as `[]` — and an `uncoveredPaths(raw, parsed)` set-difference).

A colocated `coverage.test.ts` parses **each** committed `fixtures/raw/*.json` with its matching `parse*` function and asserts `leafPaths(raw) \ leafPaths(parsed)` is a subset of an in-repo allowlist (`coverage-ignore.ts`), and that **every** allowlist entry carries a `// reason:` comment. The test fails on any raw path that is neither modeled nor explained. Runtime schemas **stay lenient** (unknown upstream keys must still not throw in prod — the S11 contract / `parse.ts` doc); this test is the strict layer.
3. The coverage test covers every `fixtures/raw/*.json` that is a **single raw upstream response** — at minimum `schedule-2026-09-05.json`, `live-823823.json`, `content-823823.json`, and `live-823823-base.json` (another live feed). `timestamps-823823.json` (a bare string array) needs only a `z.array(z.string())` parser or an explicit skip. `diffpatch-823823.json` is a derived replay envelope, **not** one upstream response — S22 types it; S23 does not.
4. The allowlist holds **≤ 25 entries total** across all fixtures — a hard ceiling so "explain everything" cannot decay into "ignore everything". The script counts entries and fails at 26+.
5. `liveData.boxscore` is fully modeled: named types for `LiveBoxscoreTeam.players[<id>]` (`person`, `position`, `status`, `stats.{batting,pitching,fielding}`, `seasonStats.{batting,pitching,fielding}`, `gameStatus`, `jerseyNumber`, `battingOrder`) and team-level `battingOrder`, `info` (label/value groups), `note`, `teamStats.{batting,pitching,fielding}`. The script greps for the type names and asserts `parse.ts` references them.

Grep of `packages/mlb-api/src/*.ts` (excluding `*.test.ts`): **no** `: any`, `as any`, `any[]`. `z.record(...)` / `z.unknown()` / `Record<string, ...>` are allowed **only** for genuine id-keyed maps (`gameData.players`, boxscore `players`) — the script permits ≤ 6 occurrences and fails above that.
8. **Composition, not repetition** — checked over the exported **types** in `packages/mlb-api/src/*.ts` (tests excluded; the zod schemas' internal nesting is not in scope):

   - no exported type name exceeds **40 characters**.
   - a colocated `shape-dedup.test.ts` asserts no two exported interfaces share **≥ 80 %** of their field names unless one `extends` / `Pick`s / `Omit`s the other, or the pair is listed with a one-line reason. The intent: `extends` / unions / `Pick` / `Omit` / small generics over near-duplicate variants.

- Naming **quality** — descriptive and idiomatic, not merely under 40 chars; whether an `extends` vs union vs discriminated-union vs generic choice is the natural one for a given shape.
- Whether a given inline shape is "specifically defensible" (a true one-off wrapper) or laziness dodging a name.
- Whether each coverage allowlist entry is genuinely not worth modeling vs. laziness. The ≤ 25 ceiling is the only mechanical guard.
- Endpoints v2's `MlbDataServer` had that are **not** in these fixtures — standings, people/players, teams, standalone boxscore/content — remain **S13**, which now inherits this coverage gate for the endpoints it adds.

### S14 — Fixture recorder from live client

**Gap:** Fixtures are hand-curated; regenerating from MLB is tribal knowledge.

**Impact:** Before S14, refreshing the app's practice-game test data from real MLB games was undocumented and done by hand. S14 impact: one command re-records that data straight from MLB, so keeping it current is now repeatable instead of tribal knowledge.

**Source:** Pillar: Dependable — tests run against real, current MLB data, re-recorded with one command. Approved by owner 2026-10-09: "The rest are all fine."

**Depends on:** S12 (S13 for standings/content fixtures)

**Scope files:** `functions/`, `README.md`, `fixtures/`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`

**Work**

0. Write `scripts/verify-S14.sh` meeting the [Verify-script contract](#verify-script-contract). Run it against current HEAD and show the nonzero exit **before** writing any product code (rule 9).

**Acceptance criteria** (checks `scripts/verify-S14.sh` performs)

1. `functions/package.json` defines a `record-fixtures` (or documented equivalent) command whose entrypoint lives under `functions/` — **not** `scripts/`, and **not** root `package.json` (root is outside this story's Scope files). The same file's dead `"seed": "tsx src/scripts/seed.ts"` script is removed or repointed — `functions/src/scripts/` does not exist at HEAD.
2. The recorder has **two recording paths**, because the `MlbStatsClient` port returns domain types only and never surfaces upstream JSON (`packages/ports/src/mlb.ts`; `HttpMlbStatsClient` parses and maps internally):
   - **raw** — writes verbatim upstream payloads, driven by an **injected `fetch`** (the existing `HttpMlbStatsClientOptions.fetchImpl` pattern), so a fake response records without network;
   - **normalized** — writes `fixtures/`-shaped JSON, driven by a **fake `MlbStatsClient`**.

### S15 — MLB API capability drift scanner

**Gap:** When Stats API adds fields/capabilities, nothing tells us. Development needs a repeatable “parse recent games → report unused/new paths” flow. S23 builds the path-coverage primitive against committed fixtures; S15 generalizes it into a runnable scanner (new / freshly recorded games, in-season) with a triage flow and docs — it does not re-invent the leaf-path diff.

### S22 — Post-game diffPatch capture + replay store

**Gap:** `games.upsert` keeps only the latest `GameSnapshot` (last-write-wins). MLB publishes a per-game timecode log (`/api/v1.1/game/{pk}/feed/live/timestamps`) and the delta between any two timecodes (`/api/v1.1/game/{pk}/feed/live/diffPatch?startTimecode=&endTimecode=`). Once a game is final we can walk that log **once**, store the ordered patch sequence plus the base feed, and reconstruct any point in the game later (variable-speed replay, rebuilding temporal state) with **no** live pipeline and **no** per-viewer MLB egress (ADR-002).

**Impact:** Before S22, once a game ended the app only kept its final snapshot — there was no way to look back at how the game unfolded moment by moment. S22 impact: a finished game's entire play-by-play can be captured once and replayed later at any point or speed, without ever contacting MLB for it again.

**Source:** Feature: Whole-game record

**Depends on:** S11 (feed payload types for the base snapshot), S12 (`HttpMlbStatsClient` + `mapLiveFeed` to reuse). Sibling to S13 — both extend the MLB client. Does **not** depend on S21: the replay store holds raw upstream patches, not BT projections.

**Prerequisite (satisfied 2026-09-07):** `fixtures/raw/` holds the recorded timecode walk for **CHC @ MIA, gamePk 823823, 2026-09-05**, captured out-of-band from `statsapi.mlb.com` (the Verify-script contract forbids network and the recorder is S14). Committed byte-exact where raw, derived where noted; `fixtures/raw` is in `.prettierignore`. Re-record with the same upstream URLs if stale:

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `fixtures/raw/timestamps-823823.json` | verbatim `/api/v1.1/game/823823/feed/live/timestamps` — 554 timecodes |
| `fixtures/raw/live-823823-base.json` | verbatim `/api/v1.1/game/823823/feed/live?timecode=<first timecode>` — the base the chain roots at (`Preview` state, ~2h before first pitch) |
| `fixtures/raw/diffpatch-823823.json` | 553-entry array, one per adjacent timecode pair: `{ startTimecode, endTimecode, diff }` where `diff` is the RFC6902 op list from `/feed/live/diffPatch` (many are `[]`). ~15 near-duplicate 2s-apart pairs that MLB returns a full feed for instead of a patch are stored as a computed minimal add/remove/replace diff with `"rebased": true` |

## Live data plane — ADR-002 ingest + client freshness

Aligned with [ARCHITECTURE §1 / ADR-002](./ARCHITECTURE.md#1-foundational-data-topology-accepted-direction): MLB egress is **backend-only** and scales with **game windows**, not viewer count. Clients read **BT**. Live feel comes from **BT freshness + delivery**—**not** per-tab MLB. Per [ADR-020](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-020--live-delivery--cadence-durable-objects-accepted-2026-10-18) / [ADR-022](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-022--idempotent-updates-accepted-2026-10-18) (2026-10-18): a per-game **ingest** Durable Object writes Postgres, then publishes versioned updates to **hub** object(s) that push one-way over hibernated WebSockets, in-window games only; everything else is cached HTTP with graduated freshness ([ADR-021](./ARCHITECTURE.md#adr-021--graduated-cache-freshness-accepted-2026-10-18)).

```text
MLB  →  typed fetch (S11–S13)  →  project to BT store shapes (S21)
                                      │
            cron → ingest object per game (S48, from S16) / refresh-on-read (S17 → S47)
                                      │  apply-if-newer, versioned (S43, S46)
                                      ├─ write Postgres (S46 ports → S50 adapter)
                                      │
                                      └─ then publish  →  hub object(s) (S18)  →  one-way WebSocket  →  watched UI (S19; S20 polls the cached schedule)
```

### S21 — Project ingested MLB into durable BT store shapes

**Gap:** Today we mostly keep thin `GameSnapshot` / fixture JSON. Product needs **processed, BT-owned documents** derived from upstream (boxscore projection, play lists, media index, linescore, etc.) so UI and live delivery read a stable store—not raw Stats API trees.

**Impact:** Before S21, the app mostly stored raw, unprocessed MLB data with nothing organizing it into the app's own shapes. S21 impact: incoming MLB data is turned into organized, purpose-built records (game header, linescore, plays, box score, media) that later screens and live features can read directly, instead of every feature having to pick apart MLB's raw format itself.

**Source:** Feature: Game → Live play / linescore context; Game → Plays + pitch detail; Game → Box score; Game → Videos / highlights

### S47 — Graduated edge caching + refresh-on-read

**Gap:** ADR-021 applies the cache-lifetime ladder twice — the edge `s-maxage` and the MLB refresh-on-read — with `stale-while-revalidate`. At HEAD handlers send no `Cache-Control` and `functions/src/services/refresh.ts` uses a fixed `CACHE_TTL_MS`. `scripts/verify-S17.sh` check 1 greps `export const CACHE_TTL_MS`, so it stays as the documented floor. Inserted by the 2026-10-18 backlog review (two independent fresh-context reviewers, merged).

**Impact:** Before S47, every finished game was re-fetched from MLB every few minutes for as long as anyone looked at it. S47 impact: the longer a game goes unchanged, the longer Cloudflare serves it straight from its cache, so finished games stop costing MLB calls and database reads within hours — while a correction still shows up within two days at most.

**Source:** Feature: Daily scoreboard by date; Game → Live play / linescore context

**Depends on:** **S43** (`cacheLifetimeMs`), **S45** (Worker responses), **S46** (`lastChangedAt`).

**Scope files:** `functions/src/`, `functions/vitest.config.ts`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `README.md`, `docs/v3/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/v3/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/v3/backlog/`, `docs/v3/AUDIT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

**Parked for the owner (2026-10-30 backlog review, after S45):** on Cloudflare a Worker runs *in front of* the cache, so a `Cache-Control: s-maxage` header on a response the Worker builds is not stored at the edge by itself (Cloudflare docs, "How the cache works": *"Cloudflare Workers run before the cache"*). Two ways to get ADR-021's edge cache, and they differ in cost and behavior:

- **Workers Cache:** `"cache": { "enabled": true }` in `wrangler.jsonc` (wrangler 4.149.0's schema has it). Cloudflare then checks the cache before running the Worker, honors `Cache-Control` per RFC 9111 (`stale-while-revalidate` included), and is *"tiered by default"*, as ADR-021 asks. But *"when caching is enabled, every request to your Worker is charged at the standard Workers request rate … including requests that are normally free: static asset requests"*, which changes ADR-017's cost line.
- **Cache API** (`caches.default.match` / `put` in the Worker): no billing change, but *"The Cache API is not compatible with tiered caching"* (one data center at a time), and the Worker still runs on every request.

**Answered (owner, 2026-10-30): "Workers cache".** The edge cache is Workers Cache, so ADR-021's tiered edge cache holds as written and ADR-017's cost line now includes every request at the Workers rate (static assets too); recording that in ADR-017 is left to the next backlog review, outside this fence. New AC 6 enables it in `wrangler.jsonc`; AC 5's README line names it. Back to `todo`.

**Parked (2026-10-30, `/run-stories`, before any code): AC 3 can't be met inside this fence.** It requires `scripts/verify-S17.sh` to exit 0, but that pinned grader's Status check (`awk '/^### S17 —/,/^### S18 —/' … | grep -q …` under `set -o pipefail`) exits 141 at HEAD every time: the backlog is ordered by priority, so the S17→S18 range now also takes in S43 and S47 (~20 KB), `grep -q` quits at its first match, and `awk` gets SIGPIPE. The same class as S48's AC 6, which the 2026-10-30 review re-pointed to a test file. Needs the owner (or a review) to re-scope AC 3 — e.g. to S17's own tests (`functions/src/services/refresh.test.ts`) passing run alone.

### S19 — Web client auto-updates watched game

**Gap:** Game page is one-shot fetch; Live/Plays/etc. do not move when BT updates. ADR-020's client layer and ADR-022 add: WebSocket only, apply only newer versions, reconnect with backoff and `?since=`, refetch on a version gap, fall back to short-polling, reconnect on tab-visible / online. Re-scoped by the 2026-10-18 backlog review to the accepted ADRs; the prior text is in git history.

**Impact:** Before S19, opening a game page fetched it once and then never changed, even if the score moved. S19 impact: a game page you're watching updates itself live, catches up on its own after a dropped connection, and never jumps backward.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** adds ADR-014's "patches in place" invariant and the S54 render-count baseline.

### S20 — Scoreboard live refresh for in-window games

**Gap:** Scoreboard is static after first load.

**Impact:** Before S20, the scoreboard only showed scores as of the moment the page loaded — a game in progress looked frozen until a manual refresh. S20 impact: the scoreboard keeps in-progress games current on its own, and pauses refreshing when the tab isn't visible so it isn't wasted effort.

**Re-scoped by the 2026-10-19 design intake review:** `web/src/api/freshness.ts` already refetches active-window payloads every 15 s and TanStack pauses while the tab is hidden, so this story mostly proves existing behaviour on the rebuilt scoreboard (S66).

**Source:** Feature: Daily scoreboard by date

The scoreboard rebuild is the *Scoreboard to the ratified frames* gap-map row and must be sliced before S20 starts, or S20 refreshes a page that is then rebuilt.
